# hybrid-lab

> A slice-of-life artifact from the SuperInstance era: a modular AI
> orchestration platform (AutoGen + FastAPI + Celery + React) for running,
> watching, and shipping multi-agent writer teams.

**What this is:** A self-contained snapshot of a working hybrid AI lab we
actually ran. Planner → Executor → Refinement workers, a runs API with SSE
streaming, an autogen PR flow, a budget-aware model router, and a React
frontend to watch it all happen.

**What it isn't:** Maintained. We're not running this anymore. The shapes are
still useful — see `STATUS.md` for the salvageable primitives and the
historical context.

## Quick start

```bash
make install        # Python venv + deps + pre-commit
make run-backend    # FastAPI on :8000
make run-worker     # Celery worker (separate terminal)
make run-frontend   # React UI on :3000 (separate terminal)
```

A compose file at `backend/orchestrator/compose/docker-compose.yml` brings up
Postgres + Redis + the API if you want the whole stack in one shot.

## How to get the big pieces

This repo does **not** bundle model weights. Set `OPENAI_API_KEY` /
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in your `.env` (see `.env.example`). The agents call
out to hosted models; local-mode needs a separate model server.

## Reading order

1. `STATUS.md` — slice-of-life notes, what was good, what we kept, what's
   worth stealing.
2. `README.original.md` — the original project README, preserved verbatim.
3. `docs/` — design notes from the time (`API.md`, `AUDIT.md`,
   `IMPROVEMENTS.md`, `INDEX.md`).

## License

MIT. See `LICENSE`.

## Pointers

- `SuperInstance/hybrid-lab` — this repo
- `SuperInstance/multiagent-project-archive` — a sibling agent-system we
  archived the same week
- `SuperInstance/circuit-breaker-archive` — separate fault-tolerance lib
  the team was exploring alongside this

Take this, fork it, evolve it. No attribution required. We'd love to hear
what you build, but you owe us nothing.

# STATUS — hybrid-lab

## What this is

A modular AI orchestration platform from the SuperInstance era: an AutoGen multi-agent
"writer team" fronted by a FastAPI orchestrator, with Celery/Redis workers, a React UI,
SSE streaming, and a budget-aware model router. Built incrementally across four
milestones (Planner → Executor → Refinement → Autogen PR flow).

## What it was good at

- **End-to-end observability** of multi-agent runs: `runs` API, SSE stream, feedback
  endpoints. You could watch a Planner reason, hand off to an Executor, get refined,
  and ship a PR — all in one screen.
- **Worker discipline**: Celery tasks had explicit states (`pending/running/completed/
  failed`) and an idempotent refinement worker. Not glamorous, but the kind of plumbing
  that makes an agent system actually demoable.
- **Pre-commit + CI hygiene** that was ahead of its time: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`,
  `.flake8`, `pyproject.toml` lint config, Makefile targets, GitHub Actions workflows
  for lint+test+build. The boring stuff you wish your team had.
- **Model routing policy + budget cap** wired in from day one (`MODEL_BUDGET_MONTHLY`,
  per-provider routing in `backend/app/...`). Many agent labs bolted this on later.

## Why we moved on

A wave of hosted agent platforms landed (managed orchestration, hosted vector stores,
turnkey eval), and the total integration surface of "Celery + Redis + Postgres + React
+ AutoGen + a custom adapter" became heavier than the problem we were solving. The
team's energy went toward a different abstraction for agent programs.

## What's here vs. upstream

| Aspect | This repo | Notes |
|--------|-----------|-------|
| Branch | `master` (preserved) | Last meaningful commit: `153a42b infra: add autogen PR flow` |
| Size | ~1.3 MB | Small on disk — most of the value is in design choices, not LOC |
| Secrets | None (only `.env.example` with placeholders) | |
| License | MIT (added at publication) | Original repo had none |
| Modified files | 11 committed changes + 11 new files | Restored to a clean push below |

## Salvageable pieces (what to steal)

- **`backend/app/runs/` and `sse_streaming`** — the pattern of "every agent run is a
  row you can rewind" is reusable. Cheap to copy-paste into a new FastAPI scaffold.
- **`infra/autogen_pr.py`** — the autogen PR flow (open PR, wait for review, merge)
  is a creative agentic primitive that fits a lot of "AI writes code" workflows.
- **`workers/tasks.py` state machine** — explicit state changes between planner →
  executor → refinement, with rollback hooks. Useful whenever you want a *traceable*
  multi-agent pipeline.
- **`backend/app/circuit_breaker.py`** — added during the push prep; the team was
  already reaching for fault tolerance between agents (and shipping a separate
  `circuit-breaker` Go lib, which is also archived).

## How to use it

```bash
make install        # sets up Python venv, deps, pre-commit
make run-backend    # FastAPI on :8000
make run-worker     # Celery worker
make run-frontend   # React UI on :3000
```

An orchestrator compose file lives at
`backend/orchestrator/compose/docker-compose.yml` if you want Postgres+Redis+API in
one shot.

## How to get the big pieces

This repo deliberately does **not** bundle model weights. The agents assume access to
OpenAI / Anthropic via API keys in `.env`. Local-mode (`MODEL_PROVIDER=local`) would
need a separate model server; nothing here will fetch weights for you.

## Provenance

Archived from `~/agent/hybrid-lab` on a local workstation. Curated and pushed to
`SuperInstance/hybrid-lab` on 2026-09 as part of the SuperInstance slice-of-life
archive — preserving the design and the working tree so others can fork and evolve.

Take this, fork it, evolve it. No attribution required. We'd love to hear what you
build, but you owe us nothing.
